purpose: First-quarter wave slice for the tenth Ruleset Card — the §1.3 generic-colo landlord card 'Amps and Aisles' / 'Cage 7' / 'The Landlord's Grid', the first card to ship founded on its OWN verbatim dominant verb, Negotiate, blessed onto the tier-extension roster by ADR-0014 #D1 (10 of the 20-type launch canon, OD-14(a)). Slice shape mirrors the nine shipped g1 siblings: a reconnaissance opening on a floor whose doors are its product, the tenant flood as the surprise-with-composition beat (the catastrophe rents by the cabinet AND draws amps), a hollow-quiet trough where the enemy is the dark cabinet still holding committed amps, and a finale built on the line's authored cruelty ('a tenant trips a shared breaker and the cascade of darkness goes through other people's racks' + 'do you evict a customer paying 30% of your revenue?', §1.3). waves.title: key.wave.1
waves.note: Rule (b) honoured: first wave of any level ALWAYS <=40% of par (§1.7). Cold Start Minute governs the first 90s of sim-time: handover no threat, one FREE conversion, signature constraint asserts harmlessly with telegraph (§1.9). On this line the harmless assertion is a drizzle of clipboards at the fence line and calls to the desk verifying deliveries nobody scheduled — the quarter opens with a clean shortest bar, a badge reader blinking green, and the only strangers paying attention to the building are the ones with questions that are not questions (§1.3's mantrap, §3.3's tour-to-contract funnel still filling the pipeline).

waves.title: key.wave.2
waves.note: Rising floor beat one — the ROUTINE catastrophe, and it is a tenant transacting. Two-Front (§2.24): the ticket hydra (Swarm — 'a request to reboot rack 7 that means something different to everyone involved', §1.3 verbatim; the registry's one swarm-on-hands engine re-framed onto this line's named combat, 'a ticket and conversation system... this is the level's combat') spends hands on the negotiation desk, while the chargeback swarm (Swarm — billed overages disputed as a crowd, the non-payer's ledger made mechanical) spends cash on the same cabinets. Two tenants, two instruments, one lesson of wave two: the enforce ladder is only power if someone at the desk can climb it while answering the phone.
waves.entropyNote: entropy budget here = f(estate age x size x (1 - maintenance spend)), NOT wave number (§2.24) — on this line maintenance spend IS the metering and the ladder discipline, and the card prices the forgetting twice: the derate dispute as the purchase, the blocklist as the unforgiven version (§1.3).

waves.title: key.wave.3
waves.note: Rule (c): 30% is 50% below the preceding peak (60%) — >=45% satisfied. Dips are where the player builds (§1.7): the clamp meters, the circuit map, the escalator ledger all get their window here. But on the colo line the quiet is the bill: the residents live there, phantom cabinets hold committed amps against a ramp nobody started, and the mesh row goes grey one hexagon at a time — '16 empty cabinets of stranded capacity for a year' (§ramp law verbatim). Two fronts: concurrency x reputation — the hoarder's dark rows read as sellable headroom while the spiral makes the emptiness itself the story the tours stop telling, and the untouchable rack keeps drawing in the one place the law says you cannot say no.

waves.title: key.wave.4
waves.note: Compound-wave exemplar, colo variant: the hot aisle and the flood window land together — a tenant's switch blocks the airflow and the whole row's fans climb (Debuffer debuts here, the every-4th-wave NEW ROLE beat; unseen in waves 1-3, the registry's one throttle-everyone mechanic re-framed onto cooling per bundle threats._todo), while the shared upstream carries a tenant's incoming flood (Tank — 'a bulletproof-host tenant gets the ENTIRE BUILDING's IP space blocklisted', §1.3 verbatim) and the collateral darkens the neighbouring rows left-to-right the way the Tier-4 row draws it. Two fronts: bandwidth (the trunk — someone else's bad day arriving at the meet-me room at line rate) x concurrency (the aisle — every throttled rack shortens everyone's bar; tonight's throughput is measured in litres of air). secondIncident inside the same window because on a shared floor one area-of-effect event is always two landlords' problems.
waves.secondIncident: thermal-throttle dispute arrives inside the flood window -> 1.8x multiplier applies (stated openly in the Codex, §2.24).

waves.title: key.wave.5
waves.note: The finale is the building's word made public property, spent from both sides at once: the ladder arrives as instruments not fists (Swarm — disputed overages, chargebacks, the notice-warning-cap-disable sequence run in reverse by tenants with lawyers, 'each rung has a legal cost and a relationship cost', §1.3 verbatim), and the spiral keeps darkening the mesh row the tours now have to walk past (Healer/Spawner) — every grey hexagon somebody's renewal negotiation, the blocklisted building's ledger finally matching its empty cabinets. Hard wave draws TWO fronts — cash x reputation — per §2.24: the tenants' counter-word and the building's word. Win check: the shortest bar held, the breaker never tripped, the flood never became the headline, and the eviction question answered with a signature instead of a silencer.
waves.triageWindow: after any catastrophic failure in this wave: arrivals queue visibly outside, patience draining, hands freed 30s (§1.7).
